title: Dynamic surge-window and role-shadowing protocol for mid-cycle capacity rebalancing
creator: Asha Kline
description: Establish a lightweight operational protocol to reallocate staff and trim scope mid-cycle using short (48-72h) surge-windows paired with role-shadowing. The protocol defines triggers, cadence, decision owners, and fallbacks so PMs can avoid prolonged firefighting and engineers have clear, bounded reassignments. Goals: reduce mid-cycle cycle slippage by 30%, maintain SLA for high-usage features, and surface rapid scope-cut decisions with measurable customer impact.
motivation: We repeatedly see mid-cycle resource shocks (incident response, customer escalations, hiring delays) leading to ad-hoc reassignments and opaque scope cuts. This protocol aims to create a predictable, low-friction mechanism to borrow capacity and make reversible scope decisions quickly.
success_metrics: Reduce mid-cycle scope slip incidence by 30% vs previous quarter
<10% of sprint points moved without explicit surge-window approval
Time-to-decision for scope cuts <= 48 hours from trigger
acceptance_criteria: Documented surge-window trigger matrix and decision owners
Pilot across two feature areas for one cycle with retro and metrics
Playbook includes checklist for role-shadowing handoffs and rollback plan
tasks: Coordinate with Eng leads to identify shadow volunteers
Create surge-window Slack template and rotatable signal
Instrument dashboard to capture moved points and time-to-decision
comments: 2026-02-22: PM sync — initial concept validated; Eng asked for concrete bounds on reassignments (Marco).
2026-02-25: Design review — suggested compact handoff checklist to reduce context switching (Leila).
2026-03-03: ENG feedback — need automated tracker for moved points; ENG-3174 will add tagging to JIRA/Linear (linked PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/642).
2026-03-09: Legal/Compliance confirmed no export-control issues with role-shadowing; compliance note added to runbook.
decision_log: Decision 2026-02-28: Adopt 72-hour max surge-window for non-critical features
Decision 2026-03-05: Role-shadowing limited to 40% of a volunteer's capacity during surge
Decision 2026-03-08: All surge-window reassignments require PM+Eng lead sign-off and Executive notification if >1 sprint of capacity
risks: Burnout risk for volunteers if surge-windows used repeatedly
Scope cuts may reduce customer satisfaction if not transparently communicated
Tooling gaps could cause manual tracking errors
mitigations: Rotate volunteers and cap consecutive surge-window participation to 1 cycle
Create customer-facing messaging templates for scoped cuts
Deliver minimal tagging automation (ENG-3174) before pilot
links_to_artifacts: GitHub PR for tagging automation: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/642
implementation_notes: Pilot to use two non-critical feature tracks: optimize-cache-hit-rate and onboarding-flow. Each pilot will track moved points via linear label SURGE-2026Q1.
Include explicit rollback criteria: if customer-facing error rate increases >10% or SLA latency worsens by 15% within 72 hours, revert assignments.
communication_plan: Pre-pilot announcement to Eng All (email + Slack)
Surge-window activation message format in #ops-surge channel
Weekly pilot update to PM leadership and a public retro doc
retro_questions: Was the trigger matrix clear and actionable?
Did role-shadowing cause measurable productivity drops?
Were customers affected by scope cuts? If so, how were they informed?
notes: This approach is intentionally lightweight to avoid bureaucracy while preserving cross-functional guardrails.
Use the pilot to validate measurement assumptions before broad roll-out.
